headline: Booze kills 17,000 in Uganda, costs country $3billion per year
summary: Research released by the Uganda Alcohol Policy Alliance estimates alcohol-related harm kills 17,000 people annually. The economic cost of excessive consumption is put at Shs11 trillion, about $2.95 billion, a year.
why: Alcohol taxation and regulation affect beverage producers and public health spending, so estimates of national costs can inform policy debates.
